correctness.rationale: For each contiguous active-block partition, strict KKT multipliers realize the corresponding blockwise weighted mean Jacobian. Single-jump functions form the ℓ_1 basis of path variation, so the exact local seminorm is its largest step-column gain. One pooled block crossing a step yields the two-boundary weighted chord of cumulative observation masses. The maximum of the chord gains is the least concave majorant sampled at all edges. Continuity and finite piecewise-linearity bound every two-input segment; an open active-set neighborhood attains the largest gain. Boundary blocks and arbitrary positive masses/weights are included. The standalone exact-rational checker independently compares 4,064 local partitions, constructs 112 KKT witnesses, and stress-tests 1,394 PAVA pairs; finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: An exact, attained quantitative formula for the weighted two-input total-variation Lipschitz modulus of path isotonic regression is not stated or entailed by the inspected order-isotonicity, NUNA contractivity, cyclic-cover variation, or coordinate-norm results. Qualitative concavity as a contractivity criterion may be obtainable from known general averaging principles, and is not counted as an independent new theorem. The novelty assessed here is the full above-one least-concave-majorant amplification profile for arbitrary positive masses and weights. Completeness of historical literature cannot be certified.
residual_risks: Older unindexed isotonic regression/BV stability literature might contain an equivalent chord-envelope identity or a broader theorem with it as a corollary.
The contractivity criterion itself is related to known averaging tests; only the exact amplification and matched witnesses form the priority claim.
No independent historical-priority or mathematical audit has occurred.

A general representation of isotonic regression as slopes of a convex minorant could yield the result under a stronger, not-yet-inspected estimate on derivative variations; the available nodal-minorant estimate does not do so.

value.rationale: The exact quantitative two-input weighted-variation stability of shape-constrained least-squares regression is a motivated invariant, especially for irregular sample masses and edge sensitivities. Unlike a binary contractivity test, the upper concave-hull ratio determines the magnitude of expansion for every nonconcave weight profile, identifies extremizing single-jump inputs, and gives the pointwise minimal stabilizing weight enlargement. It can be evaluated using a one-dimensional upper-hull algorithm rather than enumerating exponentially many active sets. Four-site sharp amplification two and arbitrary small weight-valley divergence demonstrate substantive nontrivial behavior.
